test_title: PYST 47: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 03 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In a State government, a minister holds office:

options.text: during the pleasure of the Governor
as long as they enjoy the confidence of the State Legislative Council
during the pleasure of the President

solution:
The correct answer is __**During the pleasure of the Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the parliamentary system of India, ministers at the state level hold office during the pleasure of the Governor as per **Article 164(1)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor exercises this pleasure on the advice of the Chief Minister, who must have the confidence of the State Legislative Assembly.
 
• The term "pleasure of the Governor" signifies that a minister can be removed if the Governor, acting on the advice of the Chief Minister, deems it necessary.
 
• Although the Governor is the constitutional head of the state, real executive power lies with the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• Ministers hold office as long as they maintain the confidence of the majority in the State Legislative Assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary System of Governance**

 
 
• India follows a parliamentary system of governance where the executive is accountable to the legislature.
 
• The Governor, as the constitutional head of the state, acts on the advice of the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers for executive decisions.
 
• The system ensures checks and balances between the executive and legislature for effective governance.
